claims.title: Legendary founding of Gojoseon
claims.summary: According to the Samguk yusa, the mythical Dangun establishes Gojoseon, traditionally regarded as the first Korean kingdom; the date is commemorated as National Foundation Day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-2333bce-legendary-founding-of-gojoseon, claim TL:KOR:event:2333bce:legendary-founding-of-gojoseon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Gojoseon to Han China
claims.summary: The Han dynasty conquers Gojoseon and establishes commanderies in the north, fragmenting the peninsula into smaller competing states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-108bce-fall-of-gojoseon-to-han-china, claim TL:KOR:event:108bce:fall-of-gojoseon-to-han-china, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Emergence of the Three Kingdoms
claims.summary: Silla, Goguryeo, and Baekje take shape as the three dominant kingdoms of the peninsula, each later adopting Buddhism and centralized rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-57bce-emergence-of-the-three-kingdoms, claim TL:KOR:event:57bce:emergence-of-the-three-kingdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Introduction of Buddhism
claims.summary: Buddhism is officially adopted in Goguryeo and spreads through the kingdoms, becoming a major force in art, statecraft, and religious life.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-372-introduction-of-buddhism, claim TL:KOR:event:372:introduction-of-buddhism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Silla unifies the peninsula
claims.summary: Allied with Tang China, Silla conquers Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668, then expels the Tang, achieving the first unification of Korea under native rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-668-silla-unifies-the-peninsula, claim TL:KOR:event:668:silla-unifies-the-peninsula, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bulguksa and Seokguram built
claims.summary: Unified Silla constructs the Bulguksa temple and the Seokguram grotto near Gyeongju, masterpieces of Buddhist art later inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-751-bulguksa-and-seokguram-built, claim TL:KOR:event:751:bulguksa-and-seokguram-built, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wang Geon founds Goryeo
claims.summary: The general Wang Geon establishes the Goryeo dynasty at Kaesong; by 936 he reunifies the peninsula, giving rise to the Western name Korea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-918-wang-geon-founds-goryeo, claim TL:KOR:event:918:wang-geon-founds-goryeo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mongol invasions begin
claims.summary: Mongol armies invade Goryeo; after prolonged resistance from Ganghwa Island, Korea submits to Yuan overlordship for roughly a century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1231-mongol-invasions-begin, claim TL:KOR:event:1231:mongol-invasions-begin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tripitaka Koreana completed
claims.summary: Goryeo Buddhists carve the entire Buddhist canon onto more than 80,000 woodblocks as a prayer for deliverance from the Mongols, a printing landmark preserved at Haeinsa.

claims.title: Fall of Goryeo
claims.summary: Weakened by factionalism and Mongol decline, Goryeo is overthrown by the general Yi Seong-gye, who founds the Joseon dynasty.

claims.title: Joseon dynasty founded
claims.summary: Yi Seong-gye establishes the Joseon dynasty, adopts Neo-Confucianism as state ideology, and soon moves the capital to Hanyang (Seoul).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1392-joseon-dynasty-founded, claim TL:KOR:event:1392:joseon-dynasty-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Creation of hangul
claims.summary: King Sejong the Great sponsors the Korean alphabet, completed in 1443 and promulgated in 1446 to make literacy accessible to ordinary people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1443-creation-of-hangul, claim TL:KOR:event:1443:creation-of-hangul, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese (Imjin) invasions repelled
claims.summary: Toyotomi Hideyoshi's forces invade Korea; resistance led by Admiral Yi Sun-sin and his turtle ships, with Ming Chinese aid, ultimately drives them out.

claims.title: Korea made a Japanese protectorate
claims.summary: After defeating Russia, Japan imposes a protectorate treaty stripping Korea of its diplomatic sovereignty, a prelude to full annexation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1905-korea-made-a-japanese-protectorate, claim TL:KOR:event:1905:korea-made-a-japanese-protectorate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese annexation of Korea
claims.summary: Japan formally annexes Korea, ending the Joseon dynasty and more than five centuries of Korean monarchy and beginning 35 years of colonial rule.

claims.title: Annexation and colonial government
claims.summary: Japan installs a Government-General in Seoul, ruling Korea through military and police power and beginning systematic economic exploitation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1910-annexation-and-colonial-government, claim TL:KOR:event:1910:annexation-and-colonial-government, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: March First Movement
claims.summary: A Declaration of Independence sparks nationwide demonstrations by some two million Koreans; the peaceful protests are violently suppressed with thousands killed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1919-march-first-movement, claim TL:KOR:event:1919:march-first-movement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Korean Provisional Government formed
claims.summary: Korean nationalists establish a Provisional Government in exile in Shanghai to coordinate the independence struggle against Japanese rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of South Korea: A peninsula of ancient kingdoms, half a century of colonization and fratricidal war, and a startling rise from ruin to global cultural powerhouse.", terralore.co/country/KOR/chronicle#ev-1919-korean-provisional-government-formed, claim TL:KOR:event:1919:korean-provisional-government-formed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Forced labor and wartime mobilization
claims.summary: As the Pacific War expands, Japan conscripts hundreds of thousands of Koreans for forced labor and military service and coerces women into sexual slavery.

claims.title: Rusk and Bonesteel propose the 38th parallel
claims.summary: During an overnight meeting in John McCloy's Pentagon office, US Army officers Dean Rusk and Charles Bonesteel are asked to retire to an adjoining room and propose where US forces should accept Japan's surrender in Korea. They recommend the 38th parallel to include Seoul in the American area, though it lay further north than US forces could reach if the Soviet Union disagreed (Rusk's own later account, 1950).

claims.title: Stalin does not object to General Order No. 1
claims.summary: General Order No. 1, which assigns the Japanese surrender in Korea north of 38 degrees north latitude to Soviet forces and south of it to US forces, is approved by President Truman on 17 August. In his 16 August reply Stalin writes that he has no objection in principle to the order, asking only for changes concerning the Kuril Islands and northern Hokkaido; Rusk later recalled being surprised that the Soviet Union accepted the parallel.

claims.title: American forces land at Incheon
claims.summary: MacArthur's Proclamation No. 1 (7 September) assumes military government over Korea south of 38 degrees north latitude. A small advance party of the US XXIV Corps had landed at Kimpo airfield near Seoul on 4 September; the bulk of the corps lands at Incheon and enters Seoul on 8 September.

claims.title: Election in the south
claims.summary: Elections for a National Assembly are held in South Korea, with an estimated 80 percent of eligible voters taking part; the North does not take part or recognize the result, and the UN commission is barred from the North. The UN Temporary Commission on Korea reports the results valid.

claims.summary: US and ROK units withdraw behind the Naktong River into a rectangle nearly 100 miles from north to south and about 50 miles from east to west around Pusan, where the Eighth Army commander orders that there will be no further retreat.

claims.summary: An armistice halts the fighting near the 38th parallel and creates the Demilitarized Zone; no peace treaty is signed, freezing the division to the present day.

claims.title: The Demilitarized Zone is defined
claims.summary: The armistice, signed at Panmunjom by Lt. Gen. William K. Harrison Jr. for the UN Command and Gen. Nam Il for the Korean People's Army and the Chinese People's Volunteers, fixes a military demarcation line and has both sides withdraw two kilometres from it, making a buffer zone about four kilometres wide. The line follows the positions held at the end of the fighting, not the 38th parallel; the coast-to-coast length is given as 238 kilometres by National Geographic.
